author: luna_seed_author
reviewNotes: Administrative Licensing Law Art.57 uses acceptance chronology only when multiple applications satisfy the statutory conditions and no special law supplies another order; distinction between filing and acceptance is correct. Generic hold retained because no sector-specific rule supplied.

author: luna_seed_author
reviewNotes: Administrative Licensing Law Arts.58–59 prohibit licensing/inspection fees and charge for application-form text absent statutory/regulatory exception; distinction from third-party services is appropriate.

author: luna_seed_author
reviewNotes: Administrative Licensing Law Art.61 requires recording, signatures, archive and public access; explanation appropriately preserves secrecy/privacy limits through other disclosure rules.

author: luna_seed_author
reviewNotes: Administrative Licensing Law Art.66 is limited to natural-resource development/public-resource use duties and imposes a correction order with no universal fixed number of days; regional/sector facts remain held.

author: luna_seed_author
reviewNotes: Administrative Licensing Law Art.67 covers public-interest market-entry sectors and national service/tariff standards; it does not set a city transit fare, so local tariff schedule hold is correctly retained.

author: luna_seed_author
reviewNotes: Art.67 restricts unauthorized closure of public-interest licensed operators, but the analysis says fuel/gas-specific penalties require sector and local rule verification; hold retained.

author: luna_seed_author
reviewNotes: Art.69 properly distinguishes revoke grounds, public-interest exception and lawful compensation; unlawful acquisition does not create protected reliance. Current article mapping checked.

author: luna_seed_author
reviewNotes: The analysis distinguishes affected third parties and licensees’ compensation routes, requires injury/causal nexus and flags bad-faith claimant limits under the Supreme Court administrative-license case rule; hold remains pending full facts.

author: luna_seed_author
reviewNotes: Administrative Licensing Law Arts.78–80 correctly separate false application from a license already obtained by fraud/bribery and apply the one-year versus three-year reapplication bars to covered safety matters.
